faqs.question: What is Arium Advance EDI used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Type 2 pure water system used for microbiological media and reagent preparation, chemical analysis and synthesis solutions, histology, ELISA and RIA, buffer and pH solution preparation, and feeding laboratory instruments.

faqs.question: What water quality does Arium Advance EDI produce?
faqs.answer: Type 2 pure water with a resistivity of 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently at rates up to 10 L/h.

faqs.question: What is electrodeionization and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: EDI removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than a depleting exchange capacity, which is what allows water quality to stay consistent instead of declining across a service interval.

faqs.question: What contaminants does the system remove?
faqs.answer: Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the potable feed water, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield.

faqs.question: Does Arium Advance EDI produce Type 1 ultrapure water?
faqs.answer: No. It produces Type 2 pure water. Where Type 1 is also needed, this system can feed a downstream ultrapure polisher, or a combined system covering both grades may be the better fit.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-function display responds to a light touch through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?
faqs.answer: Three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so it fits the space actually available rather than requiring space to be cleared.

faqs.question: Does it extend the life of downstream systems?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with consistent Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

faqs.question: What production rates are available?
faqs.answer: 5 L/h and 10 L/h, depending on the configuration selected.

Arium Advance EDI works differently. Patented electrodeionization runs continuously, holding Type 2 pure water at 5 to 15 MΩ·cm at production rates up to 10 L/h, connected straight to the potable feed. sections.eyebrow: Continuous EDI and Consistent Water Quality
sections.title: Continuous EDI and Consistent Water Quality
body: Electrodeionization removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than depleting a fixed pool of exchange capacity, which is why purity holds instead of declining as a cartridge would.
That continuity is what makes 5 to 15 MΩ·cm a working range rather than a peak figure — the water produced late in a service interval matches the water produced early in it.
The highest ion retention rates come alongside an optimum yield of purified water, so purity isn't achieved by rejecting an unreasonable proportion of the feed.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are all removed reliably, covering the contaminant classes that most commonly compromise media preparation and analytical solution work.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed with this water get a guaranteed longer life, because their own polishing consumables aren't compensating for an inconsistent input.
The closed bagtank protects that consistency after production — quality achieved at the membrane isn't given back to airborne contamination in an open storage vessel.

sections.title: Automatic Backflushing and Membrane Life
body: RO membranes foul. Rejected salts, particulates, and organics accumulate on the membrane surface, and left alone that layer reduces both flux and retention performance over time.
Arium Advance RO backflushes the membrane automatically using purified water, reversing flow to lift that accumulation off the surface before it consolidates.
Because the backflush uses purified water rather than raw feed, the cleaning step doesn't reintroduce the contaminants it's meant to be removing.
Automatic means it happens on the system's schedule, not the lab's — no operator step, no reminder, no dependence on someone remembering during a busy week.
The practical result is retention performance held closer to specification across the membrane's life, and a membrane that reaches its replacement point later rather than sooner.
iJust sits alongside it, calculating optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition rather than running fixed intervals that ignore what's really happening at the membrane.
